notes: This is the only Windows package identity in the repository. It is a developer identity outside the Alpha and Stable release trains (Docs/alpha-stable-release-trains.md); Sources/SpeakCore/Resources/ReleaseTrains.json defines no Windows surface, so no Alpha or Stable Windows identity, version or feed exists yet.
Callers must supply an explicit four-part version. The builder never derives one from VERSION, BUILD_NUMBER, tags or the release-train manifest.

The package family name is derived from name and publisher. The default publisher is a placeholder for the unsigned developer package; an externally supplied signing certificate requires rebuilding with its exact subject as the publisher, which creates a different package family.

The application keeps settings, history and recordings in the real %LOCALAPPDATA%\JustSpeakToIt directory used by the portable bundle. File-system write virtualisation is disabled so packaged writes are neither redirected into package-private storage nor deleted on uninstall. This needs the unvirtualizedResources restricted capability, which sideloading permits without Store approval.
maxVersionTested is the Windows build on which the lifecycle job actually executes (Windows Server 2022, build 20348). Raise it only with a receipt from a newer build.

Each package carries one processor architecture, taken from the verified runtime bundle it is built from: x64 or arm64. Both are the same developer identity; Windows installs only the package matching the PC, and a family may later move to an .msixbundle holding both but not back.
